notToBeConfusedWith.name: Triple sec
notToBeConfusedWith.note: A drier, usually clear orange liqueur; curaçao is made from bitter Curaçao orange peel and is typically darker and rounder in flavour.

generalSubstitutes.note: Trades the orange peel character for a stone-fruit one and is considerably drier, so the drink loses both its citrus top note and some of its sweetness.

forms.label: Standard, e.g. Pierre Ferrand Dry Curaçao
forms.sourceId: Pierre Ferrand Dry Curaçao, retailer product pages
forms.sourceNote: Strength taken as Pierre Ferrand Dry Curaçao's own 40% ABV, the modern reference bottle for a Mai Tai and consistently stated across retailer listings of the product. No sugar or energy figure is carried: neither Pierre Ferrand nor the older De Kuyper and Bols orange curaçaos this record also stands in for publish one, and the few third-party figures found for them disagree by a wide margin, so the figure is omitted rather than estimated. Density is the sweetened-liqueur class from density-classes.json, marked estimated, because no liquid-measure source exists for this product.
